scope: Presentation of registry-device findings in Open issues; no settings or library behavior changes
task: Scan the affected device, reported problem and its opening time, then open the existing device workflow
user_benefit: Single-issue devices use a compact two-line row, with one View action alongside. Useful distinct entity names remain visible.
disclosure: Existing integration expansion and device View are retained; no new navigation or disclosure.

visual_review.desktop: 1440px light: inspected device names, compact condition/time lines, multi-finding rows and action placement.
visual_review.phone: 390px dark: inspected wrapping, readable entity identities and reachable 44px View controls.
visual_review.note: Inspected captures precede correction of fixture expectations; later reports confirm the same layout passes. Element registration was subsequently advanced and covered by upgrade tests.

scoped_path.controls: Expand integrations, device findings, keyboard open, search, sort, Show more and refresh
scoped_path.expected: Each registry device is named once above its independent findings; standalone and shared issues remain reachable, original action targets are preserved and browsing never saves settings.
evidence: issues/1440px/light: device-issues.html (1440px, light): Synthetic backend; existing fixture uses DOM-scripted interactions. This is not real Home Assistant acceptance. Three integration families; single device heading; independent findings; equal names, standalone and shared issue identities. Focusable device View, canonical device query, independently selected issue identities, and detail close; no attention action invoked. Parent-name search, three sort choices, 40-to-45 pagination and unchanged refresh retention. No queue removal controls or counts. Device, shared and standalone dialogs review their exact current availability scope with named entities immediately visible. Cancel and Close discard review without mutations or live services; current viewport fits. Issue rows omit internal grouping labels. Waiting checks and their conditions are directly visible under their device through refresh; prior vacuum error survives unavailability in list and dialog; complete scope remains visible beside acknowledgment and pause, both targeting the original issue.
